claim: On Mar 14, 2025 Kinesis Data Streams started to allow API requests over IPv6, with the option of using either IPv6 or IPv4 when sending requests over dual-stack public endpoints.
question: Since when can Kinesis Data Streams be called over IPv6?

values.display: either IPv6 or IPv4 when sending requests over dual-stack public endpoints

qualifiers.condition: available in all Regions except AWS GovCloud (US) and China Regions at launch

evidence.quote: Customers now have the option of using either IPv6 or IPv4 when sending requests over dual-stack public endpoints.

evidence.heading: Amazon Kinesis Data Streams now supports Internet Protocol version 6

claim: On May 14, 2025 Kinesis Data Streams started to allow API requests over IPv6 with dual-stack AWS PrivateLink interface VPC endpoints, extending IPv6 compatibility that was previously available only for public endpoints.
question: Since when do Kinesis Data Streams interface VPC endpoints support IPv6?

values.display: dual-stack AWS PrivateLink interface Virtual Private Clouds (VPC) endpoints

qualifiers.scope: Kinesis Data Streams interface VPC endpoints

evidence.quote: Amazon Kinesis Data Streams now allows customers to make API requests over Internet Protocol version 6 (IPv6) with dual-stack AWS PrivateLink interface Virtual Private Clouds (VPC) endpoints. This enhancement extends IPv6 compatibility, previously available only for public endpoints, to VPC endpoints across all AWS Regions.

evidence.heading: Amazon Kinesis Data Streams expands IPv6 support to VPC endpoints

claim: On Apr 30, 2025 Kinesis Data Streams introduced support for tagging and Attribute-Based Access Control (ABAC) for enhanced fan-out consumers, so IAM policies can allow or deny specific API actions when the principal's tags match the tags on a registered consumer.
question: Since when can enhanced fan-out consumers be tagged and used in ABAC policies?

values.display: tagging and Attribute-Based Access Control (ABAC) for enhanced fan-out consumers

qualifiers.scope: Kinesis Data Streams enhanced fan-out consumers
qualifiers.condition: available in all AWS Regions, including AWS China and AWS GovCloud (US) Regions

evidence.quote: Today, Amazon Kinesis Data Streams introduces support for tagging and Attribute-Based Access Control (ABAC) for enhanced fan-out consumers.

Additionally, ABAC support for enhanced fan-out consumers allows you to use IAM policies to allow or deny specific Kinesis Data Streams API actions when the IAM principal's tags match the tags on a registered consumer.

evidence.heading: Amazon Kinesis Data Streams now supports tagging and Attribute-Based Access Control for consumers
